summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require warrant authorisation for law enforcement and intelligence agencies seeking telecommunications data, extending procedures used for stored communications to other information.
It would remove provisions allowing existing or prospective telecommunications information to be disclosed without a warrant, including specified sharing with federal police and foreign agencies.
The amendments would begin the day after Royal Assent, while retaining disclosures used to help locate missing people and extending the information covered by warrants.
changes: The Australian Security Intelligence Organisation would need warrants for access to existing and prospective telecommunications information.
Issuing authorities would have to be satisfied of additional matters before granting warrants.
Warrants would authorise access to information sent or received during the period they specified.
summary.affected: Law enforcement and intelligence agencies and people whose telecommunications information is sought, including missing persons, are affected.

speeches.speaker: Scott Ludlam
speeches.brief: The Telecommunications Amendment (Get a Warrant) Bill 2013 was introduced to amend the Telecommunications (Interception and Access) Act 1979 and passed its first reading without formalities.
